comments.text:
I hope this creator doesn't block me for saying what I honestly think.

It's amazing how far we've come. Someone sits at home, compiles other people's videos, puts their face in the corner, adds a few reactions and comments, and suddenly they're considered—or consider themselves—a content creator. What's even more surprising is that people are willing to pay monthly memberships for it. Why? I honestly don't know.

What concerns me even more is that many creators don't seem to realize they've become dependent on YouTube. They're afraid that if they stop uploading—even for a short time or if the content isn't meaningful—the algorithm will forget them. They wake up and check their analytics before they've even enjoyed their morning coffee.

To me, that's a sign of anxiety, not freedom. It's ironic to hear people talk about living freely while feeling constant pressure to feed the algorithm. Sometimes it seems they don't realize they're serving the platform instead of the other way around.
